newsitem.title: USA: ADM faces litigation in corn syrup suit.
newsitem.headline: ADM faces litigation in corn syrup suit.

text.p: Archer Daniels Midland Co, which recently settled two customer price-fixing lawsuits for $60 million, still faces the potentially costliest suit brought by buyers of high-fructose corn syrup, plaintiffs attorneys said.
Attorneys representing a class of about 2,700 plaintiffs said no settlement is expected soon in the corn syrup suit brought against ADM on grounds of alleged price fixing.
"There's nothing on the horizon right now. Everybody is posturing themselves in a litigating mode," said Laddie Montague, one of three co-lead counsels for the plaintiffs.
The high fructose corn syrup litigation is the last -- and potentially the biggest -- case brought against ADM by its customers, Montague said.
Like the class action suits involving lysine and citric acid, the corn syrup suit stems from an ongoing federal investigation into alleged price fixing.

Previously, ADM agreed to pay $25 million to settle a price-fixing case brought by buyers of lysine, a feed additive, and to pay $35 million to settle a suit brought by buyers of citric acid, a food additive.

Attorneys said plaintiffs in the high fructose corn syrup case, including food and beverage companies, are seeking treble damages for allegedly paying inflated prices. The total amount of damages being sought was not disclosed.
Soft drink giants Coca-Cola Co and PepsiCo Inc are among the plaintiffs, Montague said.
Montague said discovery is ongoing in the corn syrup suit, with a cutoff date set at the end of April, 1997. A trial date has been set for March 1998.

ADM did not comment on the corn syrup customer suit. In its annual report, filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission, ADM said it and several other companies have been named as defendants in at least 29 class action antitrust suits involving high fructose corn syrup. The suits have been consolidated in a class action.

Kenneth Adams, an attorney representing several plaintiffs including Quaker Oats Co and the Kraft Foods division of Philip Morris Cos Inc, also said a settlement in the corn syrup customer case brought against ADM is not expected in the near-term.
"We do not have any reason to plan to settle the case any time soon," Adams added.

Meanwhile, federal antitrust charges are said to be pending against ADM. Justice is pressing ADM to enter pleas to price-fixing charges in lysine, citric acid and high fructose corn syrup, according to a source close to the probe.
ADM has said it and two top executives have been informed that they are targets of the lysine investigation and indictments are being considered against them.
